settings.heading: A shirting house built on
settings.lead: Gridium is an independent shirting atelier. We design and manufacture a deliberately small catalogue of Oxfords, poplins, linens and knits — each pattern revised over years, not seasons, with family-owned European mills we visit in person.

settings.title: Proportion before decoration
settings.text: Silhouette is resolved on the pattern table. Trims come last, and only if they earn their place.

settings.title: Materials with a paper trail
settings.text: Every yarn has a mill, a batch number and a certification we can name out loud.

settings.title: Repair before replace
settings.text: Buttons, interlinings and collar stock are held for a decade so a shirt can outlive a trend cycle.

settings.statement: We are not interested in reinventing the shirt every season. We are interested in the eleventh revision of the same collar.
settings.left_text:
A wardrobe is a system, not a feed. When a shape is right — the shoulder sits where your arm actually pivots, the hem clears the hip at the correct angle — newness stops being the point. So we keep one shirt block per silhouette and spend the year improving it instead of replacing it.

The catalogue grows only when a fabric demands a new block. That is why there are six shirts here and not sixty.
settings.right_text:
Our weaving partners are family-run mills in Portugal, Belgium and Italy that we pay directly, on time, at volumes small enough to keep quality accountable. Every run is cut in a single atelier, checked by hand, and released only when the collar rolls the way the sample did.

Nothing is outsourced to an agent we have not met. If a lot fails inspection, it does not become a sale — it becomes a note on the wall.

settings.title: Architectural pattern discipline
settings.text: Every block is drafted in-house with high, pitched armholes for clean chest lines and unrestricted reach — graded across six sizes, never scaled from a medium.

settings.title: Unfused soft collar roll
settings.text: We avoid rigid synthetic fusing so collars frame the neck naturally, whether buttoned under tailoring or worn open on a Saturday.

settings.title: Permanent archive over trends
settings.text: Core silhouettes stay in production year-round, so you can reorder your exact block in a new seasonal fabric without re-learning your size.

settings.heading: One garment category. Perfected without noise.
settings.lead: Gridium began with a frustration: shirts that photographed well and behaved badly after the fourth wash. So we built a studio around the parts nobody sees — seam allowance, interlining, button shank.
settings.lead_secondary: Ten years later the method has not changed. Fewer styles, better patterns, and a mill relationship that survives a bad season.

settings.title: The first Oxford block
settings.text: Built from a tailor's reference shirt and re-graded eleven times until the shoulder stopped pulling forward.

settings.title: The first mill partnership
settings.text: Somelos wove our two-ply poplin at a volume small enough that we could reject an entire run over one crooked placket.

settings.title: Belgian flax, traced
settings.text: Masters of Linen® certification arrived with a paper trail we could publish — so we published it, lot by lot.

settings.title: The atelier opens
settings.text: Cutting and finishing moved under one roof so we could control the seams customers actually feel.

settings.title: Repairs, in perpetuity
settings.text: Buttons, interlinings and collar stock are now held for ten years. A shirt should never become waste because one stitch failed.

settings.heading: Ten years, six blocks, one standard.
settings.intro: We grew slowly on purpose. Each chapter below marks a decision that narrowed the catalogue rather than widened it.
settings.footnote: ARCHIVE: EVERY SAMPLE SINCE 2016 IS KEPT ON SITE.

settings.title: Yarn & weaving
settings.text: Long-staple cotton is spun and woven in a single mill so the lot can be traced from bale to bolt. We test shrinkage after five washes before any fabric is approved.

settings.title: Pattern & cutting
settings.text: Every block is drafted in-house and graded across six sizes. Cutters work in short runs so a crooked panel is caught in the room, not in the warehouse.

settings.title: Sewing & finishing
settings.text: Collars are single-needle set and left unfused. Buttons are whipped onto thermally locked shanks so they flex instead of cracking.

settings.title: Inspection & archive
settings.text: Two people check each shirt against the master sample. Pattern, fabric lot and machine operator are logged into the archive.

settings.heading: Patternmakers, weavers, and one very patient machinist.
settings.intro: Eleven people work on the Gridium catalogue. These are the three who sign off on a shirt before it ships.

settings.question: Why do you only make shirts?
settings.answer: Because a category is a craft. Splitting attention across trousers, knitwear and outerwear would mean abandoning the pattern revisions that make our collars sit correctly. One category, held to one standard.

settings.question: Where is a Gridium shirt made?
settings.answer: Fabric is woven by our partner mills in Portugal, Belgium, Italy and Japan. Cutting, sewing and finishing happen in our own atelier in Porto, with final inspection in New York.

settings.question: Do you repair shirts after purchase?
settings.answer: Yes. Repairs are free within the first year and at cost afterwards, for as long as we hold stock of the component. Send a note to the studio with your order number.

settings.question: Can I visit the studio?
settings.answer: The New York studio is open by appointment, Monday to Friday. Fittings include a comparison against three adjacent sizes so you leave knowing your block, not guessing at it.

settings.heading: What people ask before their first order
settings.subtext: Sizing, provenance and care — answered plainly.

settings.heading: Come see the seam allowance.
settings.text: Our New York studio keeps every sample since 2016 on the wall. Appointments are free, unhurried, and include a fitting against three adjacent sizes.
